raw_response:
I farm in Quzhou, Hebei. Everyone here grows winter wheat and summer maize on rotation — my parents did it, my neighbors do it, and I know how to do it. I have about 10 mu of land and I will plant all of it in wheat this coming October, then turn it straight into maize after the June harvest. That is just how the year goes here.

For the wheat I will buy the improved seed from the county supply station — I stopped using my own saved seed years ago because the yields were not as good. I put down compound fertilizer before plowing and then urea at the jointing stage. I irrigate about four times: before winter sets in, at greening, at jointing, and at heading. I spray herbicide in the spring and once more for rust and aphids around heading. I plow deep before seeding — the soil needs it after the maize stalks are chopped in.

For the maize I drill it straight into the wheat stubble without plowing. The seeds are hybrid —郑单958 or whatever the shop recommends that is similar. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and come back with urea when it reaches knee height. I only irrigate if it gets very dry around silking. I spray once or twice, usually for corn borer.

I expect around 450 jin of wheat per mu and maybe 550 of maize. Not the best in the county but steady enough.
